summary: MODEL_CHANGE_REQUIRED: Learner.shutdown now calls zk.shutdown(syncMode==SNAP) and ZooKeeperServer.shutdown(boolean) clears an unstarted zkDb. The reference suite was updated (SNAP/TRUNC reconciliation split, per-follower learner exit with clear and reload, leaked log-processor queues, zxid-based sync decision, NEWLEADER commit) with Update.tla/UpdateProps.tla and evidence for every property decision. The prior harness patch applied cleanly; the missing prior stateful emitter was rebuilt (schema v3). Five fresh new-revision traces, including the update's own testDiffSyncAfterSnap, pass TLC trace validation with TraceMatched; old-revision traces replay under the old semantics and reproduce the old data gap (recovered [11]). Model checking: the update's SNAP fix holds within bounds (UPD-1 exhaustive, 144,904 states, no violation; the old semantics violate). Findings: MC-1 (introduced by the update): zk.shutdown(boolean) bypasses LearnerZooKeeperServer.shutdown(), so the follower SyncRequestProcessor is never stopped or drained on learner exit; reproduced in real code (new revision fails, old passes); in the model a re-synced follower can lose a committed txn from its log or replay a stale record. MC-2 (pre-existing): the TRUNC branch has the same unpersisted in-memory window and is not covered by the SNAP-only guard. MC-3 (pre-existing): fast-forward before drain leaves re-sent records out of order. Budgeted full/residual/open/discharge campaigns found nothing beyond these, but they are LIMITED_COVERAGE, not proof.
